rust.error: document type declarations are not supported

reason: fast-xml-parser reads a document type declaration and expands the internal entities it declares; that reader (DocTypeReader.js with xml-naming and is-unsafe, about 400 lines) is not ported. Rust refuses the fragment, and that is the decided end state: the Open Packaging Conventions forbid DTDs in a package part. No tracked document has a DOCTYPE in a part the engine parses.

rust.error: a surrogate pair would be split

reason: fast-xml-parser takes the nine UTF-16 units after any '<![' as the CDATA opener, so a malformed opener can cut a character outside the BMP in half and leave a lone surrogate in the text. A Rust string cannot hold a lone surrogate. Rust refuses the fragment instead of inventing a replacement character.

JSZip has two UTF-8 decoders. Where a global Buffer exists (Node: CLI, tests, main process) it replaces each ill-formed sequence with U+FFFD, which is what Rust does and what the gate compares. Where none exists (a browser, and the sandboxed desktop renderer unless a bundler supplies one) it uses pako's decoder, which never rejects a byte: stray continuation bytes become control characters, a lead byte swallows the bytes after it, encoded surrogates stay lone surrogates, and the result depends on where JSZip's 16 KiB blocks end. The TypeScript engine therefore already reads ill-formed parts differently per host. Rust follows the Node behaviour everywhere. Every .xml and .rels entry of the tracked documents is well-formed UTF-8, so no tracked document is affected.

typescript.refused: zip rejected: part word/styles.xml cannot be inflated: TypeError

rust.refused: zip rejected: part word/styles.xml cannot be inflated: the deflate data is damaged or cut short

reason: The zip gate ends this message with the text of the error DecompressionStream rejects with. That text belongs to the host: Node 22 rejects with a TypeError whose message is empty, so the gate falls back to its name, and a browser words it differently. Rust writes one sentence of its own. The gate compares the message up to "cannot be inflated:", which is the part the TypeScript wrote.

typescript.value: <m:r><m:t xml:space="preserve">x</m:t></m:r>

reason: latexToOmml recurses once per group and the TypeScript runs until the JavaScript stack overflows, somewhere past a thousand levels depending on the host. A stack overflow in wasm ends the instance, so Rust counts the depth and refuses past 256 levels of its reader (128 nested groups). No formula a person writes is that deep; the limit is listed because the two sides answer differently between the two limits.

reason: TypeScript defect, fix pending on main. The TypeScript formats the number it is given, so a NaN or an infinity reaches the XML as the text "NaN" or "Infinity", which no schema type of that attribute or element admits (they are integers), so the part is invalid. Rust never writes a non-finite number: a value that is optional or that patches an existing one is ignored, as patchImageParagraphXml already does on both sides, and a number a builder needs is written as the floor the TypeScript clamps a size to, or as 0 for a position. Where the TypeScript result holds no NaN or Infinity, Rust gives that result.
